answer: Trading requires a live policy, and the underwriter prices each seat from how its funding, timing and counterparties correlate with the rest of the pool. A seat fed from its own purse pays the base rate; a fleet of k keys drawing from one funding jetty moves as a single exposure, so the pool's tail risk grows with k squared and the premium for the k-th seat rises with it. Reserves backing that variance are struck in quartz, and a single forged claim is the ember that burns them and reprices the whole cohort.
